Python (programming language).title: Python (programming language)
Python (programming language).summary: Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language. Its design philosophy emphasizes code readability with the use of significant indentation.

sections.History: Python was conceived by Guido van Rossum in the late 1980s and first released in 1991.
sections.Syntax and semantics: Python uses off-side rule indentation to delimit blocks rather than braces.
sections.Libraries: Python has a large standard library and a vast ecosystem including NumPy, pandas, and Django.

Guido van Rossum.title: Guido van Rossum
Guido van Rossum.summary: Guido van Rossum is a Dutch programmer best known as the creator of the Python programming language, a role for which he was the 'benevolent dictator for life' until 2018.

sections.Early life: Van Rossum was born in 1956 in the Netherlands and studied mathematics at the University of Amsterdam.
sections.Python: He began work on Python in December 1989 as a successor to the ABC language.
sections.Later career: He joined Dropbox in 2013 and later worked at Microsoft from 2020.

Machine learning.title: Machine learning
Machine learning.summary: Machine learning is a field of study in artificial intelligence concerned with the development of statistical algorithms that learn from data.

sections.Overview: Machine learning algorithms build models from sample data to make predictions or decisions.
sections.Approaches: Approaches include supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning.
sections.Applications: Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, and recommendation systems.

key_facts: Includes supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning
Powers recommendation systems and computer vision

Artificial intelligence.title: Artificial intelligence
Artificial intelligence.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is intelligence demonstrated by machines, in contrast to the natural intelligence displayed by humans and animals.

sections.History: The field was founded at the Dartmouth workshop in 1956 by John McCarthy and others.
sections.Subfields: Major subfields include machine learning, computer vision, natural language processing, and robotics.
sections.Ethics: AI ethics concerns fairness, accountability, transparency, and the alignment problem.

key_facts: Includes machine learning and computer vision

Deep learning.title: Deep learning
Deep learning.summary: Deep learning is a subset of machine learning that uses artificial neural networks with multiple layers to learn representations of data.

sections.Overview: Deep learning models use many stacked layers of nonlinear processing units.
sections.History: Key milestones include the backpropagation algorithm and the 2012 AlexNet breakthrough.
sections.Applications: Used in image recognition, speech recognition, and natural language processing.

Neural network.title: Neural network
Neural network.summary: An artificial neural network is a computational model inspired by the structure of biological neural networks in the brain.

sections.Architecture: A neural network consists of layers of interconnected nodes (neurons) with weighted connections.
sections.Training: Networks are trained by adjusting weights via backpropagation and gradient descent.
sections.Types: Common types include feedforward, convolutional, and recurrent neural networks.

Transformer (deep learning architecture).title: Transformer (deep learning architecture)
Transformer (deep learning architecture).summary: A transformer is a deep learning architecture introduced in 2017 that relies entirely on the attention mechanism, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions.

sections.Architecture: Transformers use self-attention to weigh the importance of different input tokens.
sections.History: Introduced in the 2017 paper 'Attention Is All You Need' by Vaswani et al. at Google.
sections.Impact: Transformers underpin large language models such as GPT-3 and BERT.

Natural language processing.title: Natural language processing
Natural language processing.summary: Natural language processing (NLP) is a subfield of linguistics and computer science concerned with interactions between computers and human language.

sections.Tasks: Core tasks include machine translation, sentiment analysis, and question answering.
sections.Methods: Modern NLP relies heavily on transformers and large language models.
sections.History: Early work used rule-based systems; statistical methods dominated in the 1990s and 2000s.

key_facts: GPT and BERT are landmark models

Computer vision.title: Computer vision
Computer vision.summary: Computer vision is a field of artificial intelligence that enables computers to derive meaningful information from digital images and videos.

sections.Tasks: Tasks include image classification, object detection, and segmentation.
sections.Methods: Convolutional neural networks became dominant after the AlexNet result in 2012.
sections.Applications: Used in facial recognition, medical imaging, and autonomous vehicles.

key_facts: Field of AI for images and video

Large language model.title: Large language model
Large language model.summary: A large language model (LLM) is a neural network with billions of parameters trained on vast text corpora to generate and understand human language.

sections.Architecture: Most modern LLMs use the transformer architecture.
sections.Training: LLMs are trained via self-supervised learning then refined with reinforcement learning from human feedback.
sections.Examples: Notable examples include GPT-3, GPT-4, and BERT.

GPT-3.title: GPT-3
GPT-3.summary: GPT-3 (Generative Pre-trained Transformer 3) is a large language model released by OpenAI in 2020 with 175 billion parameters.

sections.Architecture: GPT-3 is an autoregressive transformer language model.
sections.Capabilities: It demonstrated strong few-shot learning across many language tasks.
sections.Impact: GPT-3 powered the original ChatGPT and catalyzed widespread interest in generative AI.

ChatGPT.title: ChatGPT
ChatGPT.summary: ChatGPT is a conversational AI chatbot released by OpenAI in November 2022, built on the GPT-3.5 and later GPT-4 large language models.

sections.Release: ChatGPT launched on November 30, 2022 and reached 100 million users in two months.
sections.Technology: It is fine-tuned from GPT-3.5/GPT-4 using reinforcement learning from human feedback.
sections.Impact: ChatGPT sparked a global wave of interest in generative AI and rival products.

key_facts: Reached 100 million users in two months

OpenAI.title: OpenAI
OpenAI.summary: OpenAI is an American artificial intelligence research organization founded in 2015, known for developing the GPT family of large language models and ChatGPT.

sections.History: OpenAI was founded in December 2015 by Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Ilya Sutskever, and others.
sections.Products: Its products include GPT-3, GPT-4, ChatGPT, DALL-E, and Sora.
sections.Governance: Microsoft is a major investor; Sam Altman is the CEO.

NumPy.title: NumPy
NumPy.summary: NumPy is a library for the Python programming language that adds support for large, multi-dimensional arrays and matrices, along with a large collection of high-level mathematical functions.

sections.Features: NumPy provides an n-dimensional array object and broadcasting functions.
sections.History: It was created in 2005 by Travis Oliphant by merging Numeric and Numarray.
sections.Ecosystem: NumPy underpins the scientific Python stack including SciPy and pandas.

PyTorch.title: PyTorch
PyTorch.summary: PyTorch is an open-source machine learning framework developed by Meta's AI Research lab, used for applications such as computer vision and natural language processing.

sections.Features: PyTorch provides dynamic computational graphs and strong GPU acceleration.
sections.History: It was released in 2016 and is based on the Torch library.
sections.Ecosystem: PyTorch is widely used in deep learning research and powers Hugging Face Transformers.

TensorFlow.title: TensorFlow
TensorFlow.summary: TensorFlow is a free and open-source software library for machine learning and artificial intelligence, developed by the Google Brain team.

sections.Features: TensorFlow supports deep learning with static computational graphs and production deployment via TensorFlow Serving.
sections.History: It was released by Google in 2015, evolving from the earlier DistBelief system.
sections.Ecosystem: Keras is the high-level API integrated into TensorFlow.

Algorithm.title: Algorithm
Algorithm.summary: An algorithm is a finite sequence of well-defined instructions used to solve a class of problems or perform a computation.

sections.Overview: Algorithms are unambiguous specifications for performing calculation, data processing, and automated reasoning.
sections.Complexity: Algorithm efficiency is often analyzed in terms of time and space complexity (big O notation).
sections.Examples: Common algorithms include sorting, searching, and graph traversal algorithms.

Alan Turing.title: Alan Turing
Alan Turing.summary: Alan Turing was an English mathematician, computer scientist, and cryptanalyst, widely considered a founder of theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence.

sections.Early life: Turing was born in 1912 in London and studied at Cambridge and Princeton.
sections.Codebreaking: During World War II he worked at Bletchley Park breaking German ciphers including the Enigma machine.
sections.Legacy: He proposed the Turing test and the concept of the universal Turing machine.

key_facts: Broke the Enigma cipher at Bletchley Park

Turing test.title: Turing test
Turing test.summary: The Turing test, proposed by Alan Turing in 1950, is a test of a machine's ability to exhibit intelligent behavior indistinguishable from that of a human.

sections.Definition: A human evaluator judges conversations between a human and a machine; if the machine is indistinguishable, it passes.
sections.History: Turing introduced the 'imitation game' in his 1950 paper 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence'.
sections.Criticism: Critics argue passing the test does not imply true understanding or consciousness.

Albert Einstein.title: Albert Einstein
Albert Einstein.summary: Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist, widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest scientists of all time, known for developing the theory of relativity.

sections.Early life: Einstein was born in 1879 in Ulm, Germany, and later moved to Switzerland and the United States.
sections.Relativity: He published the special theory of relativity in 1905 and the general theory in 1915.
sections.Nobel Prize: He received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for his discovery of the photoelectric effect.

Isaac Newton.title: Isaac Newton
Isaac Newton.summary: Sir Isaac Newton was an English mathematician, physicist, and astronomer, widely recognized as one of the most influential scientists, famous for his laws of motion and universal gravitation.

sections.Early life: Newton was born in 1642 in Lincolnshire, England, and studied at Cambridge.
sections.Principia: His 1687 work 'Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica' laid the foundations of classical mechanics.
sections.Legacy: He also developed calculus independently of Leibniz and made major contributions to optics.

key_facts: Formulated laws of motion and gravitation

Charles Darwin.title: Charles Darwin
Charles Darwin.summary: Charles Darwin was an English naturalist and biologist, best known for his contributions to the science of evolution and his theory of natural selection.

sections.Voyage: Darwin sailed on the HMS Beagle from 1831 to 1836, gathering evidence in the Galapagos and elsewhere.
sections.On the Origin of Species: He published his theory of evolution by natural selection in 1859.
sections.Legacy: Darwin's work established evolution as the unifying theory of the life sciences.

key_facts: Published 'On the Origin of Species' in 1859

Marie Curie.title: Marie Curie
Marie Curie.summary: Marie Curie was a Polish-born French physicist and chemist who conducted pioneering research on radioactivity, and was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.

sections.Early life: Curie was born Maria Sklodowska in 1867 in Warsaw, then part of the Russian Empire.
sections.Research: With her husband Pierre Curie she discovered the elements polonium and radium.
sections.Nobel Prizes: She won Nobel Prizes in Physics (1903) and Chemistry (1911).

key_facts: First woman to win a Nobel Prize
Won Nobel Prizes in both Physics and Chemistry

Nikola Tesla.title: Nikola Tesla
Nikola Tesla.summary: Nikola Tesla was a Serbian-American inventor and electrical engineer best known for his contributions to the design of the modern alternating current (AC) electricity supply system.

sections.Early life: Tesla was born in 1856 in the Austrian Empire (modern Croatia) and emigrated to the United States in 1884.
sections.Inventions: He developed the AC induction motor and worked for a time with Thomas Edison before their rivalry.
sections.Legacy: The SI unit of magnetic flux density, the tesla, is named after him.

key_facts: The tesla unit is named after him

World War II.title: World War II
World War II.summary: World War II was a global conflict that lasted from 1939 to 1945, involving most of the world's nations and resulting in an estimated 70-85 million deaths.

sections.Causes: The war grew out of unresolved tensions from World War I, fascist expansionism, and the invasion of Poland in 1939.
sections.Major events: Key events included the Battle of Britain, Pearl Harbor, Stalingrad, D-Day, and the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
sections.Aftermath: The war led to the founding of the United Nations and the beginning of the Cold War.

key_facts: Involved the Axis and Allied powers
Ended with atomic bombings of Japan
Led to the founding of the United Nations

Cold War.title: Cold War
Cold War.summary: The Cold War was a period of geopolitical tension between the United States and the Soviet Union and their respective allies from 1947 to 1991.

sections.Overview: The Cold War was characterized by proxy wars, arms races, and the threat of nuclear conflict.
sections.Key events: Major events included the Berlin Blockade, the Cuban Missile Crisis, and the construction and fall of the Berlin Wall.
sections.End: The Cold War ended with the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991.

key_facts: Ended with the Soviet Union's collapse

French Revolution.title: French Revolution
French Revolution.summary: The French Revolution was a period of radical political and societal change in France that began in 1789 and ended in the late 1790s.

sections.Causes: Causes included financial crisis, social inequality, and Enlightenment ideas.
sections.Key events: The storming of the Bastille on July 14, 1789 and the Reign of Terror were defining moments.
sections.Legacy: The Revolution abolished the monarchy and produced the Declaration of the Rights of Man.

Roman Empire.title: Roman Empire
Roman Empire.summary: The Roman Empire was the post-Republican period of ancient Rome, lasting from 27 BC to 476 AD in the west, and was one of the largest empires in history.

sections.Founding: Augustus became the first emperor in 27 BC after the fall of the Roman Republic.
sections.Expansion: At its height the empire encircled the Mediterranean and stretched from Britain to Mesopotamia.
sections.Fall: The Western Roman Empire fell in 476 AD; the Eastern (Byzantine) Empire lasted until 1453.

Industrial Revolution.title: Industrial Revolution
Industrial Revolution.summary: The Industrial Revolution was the transition to new manufacturing processes in Europe and the United States, roughly from 1760 to 1840.

sections.Origins: It began in Great Britain with mechanized textile production and the steam engine.
sections.Innovations: Key innovations included James Watt's steam engine, the spinning jenny, and the railway.
sections.Impact: It transformed agrarian societies into industrial urban ones and raised living standards over time.

Apollo 11.title: Apollo 11
Apollo 11.summary: Apollo 11 was the American spaceflight that landed the first humans on the Moon on July 20, 1969, as part of the Apollo program.

sections.Crew: The crew consisted of Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins.
sections.Landing: Armstrong and Aldrin landed the lunar module Eagle while Collins orbited in Columbia.
sections.Legacy: Armstrong's 'one small step' marked a US victory in the Space Race with the Soviet Union.

Neil Armstrong.title: Neil Armstrong
Neil Armstrong.summary: Neil Armstrong was an American astronaut and aeronautical engineer who, as commander of Apollo 11, became the first person to walk on the Moon in 1969.

sections.Early life: Armstrong was born in 1930 in Ohio and served as a naval aviator before joining NASA.
sections.Apollo 11: He commanded Apollo 11 and stepped onto the lunar surface on July 20, 1969.
sections.Legacy: After Apollo he taught at the University of Cincinnati and avoided the public spotlight.

United States.title: United States
United States.summary: The United States of America is a country primarily located in North America, consisting of 50 states, a federal district, and several territories.

sections.Geography: The US is the third-largest country by area and spans from the Atlantic to the Pacific, including Alaska and Hawaii.
sections.Government: It is a federal republic with three branches: executive, legislative, and judicial.
sections.History: Founded in 1776, it expanded across the continent and became a global superpower after World War II.

New York City.title: New York City
New York City.summary: New York City is the most populous city in the United States, located at the southern tip of New York State, and a global center for finance, culture, and media.

sections.Boroughs: The city comprises five boroughs: Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx, and Staten Island.
sections.Economy: It is home to Wall Street, the New York Stock Exchange, and the United Nations headquarters.
sections.Landmarks: Famous landmarks include the Statue of Liberty, Central Park, and Times Square.

key_facts: Global financial hub with Wall Street

London.title: London
London.summary: London is the capital and largest city of England and the United Kingdom, with a history dating back to Roman times as Londinium.

sections.History: Founded by the Romans as Londinium, London later became the center of the British Empire.
sections.Government: It hosts the UK Parliament at Westminster and the royal residence at Buckingham Palace.
sections.Landmarks: Landmarks include the Tower of London, Big Ben, and the British Museum.

Tokyo.title: Tokyo
Tokyo.summary: Tokyo is the capital of Japan and one of the most populous metropolitan areas in the world, located on the island of Honshu.

sections.History: Formerly known as Edo, it became the imperial capital in 1868 when Emperor Meiji moved his seat from Kyoto.
sections.Economy: Tokyo is a major global financial center and hosts the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
sections.Culture: It blends ultramodern skyscrapers with historic temples such as Senso-ji.

key_facts: One of the world's largest metro areas

Paris.title: Paris
Paris.summary: Paris is the capital and most populous city of France, situated on the Seine River in the north-central part of the country.

sections.History: Paris has been the capital of France since 987 and was central to the French Revolution.
sections.Culture: It is renowned for art, fashion, and cuisine, and hosts the Louvre museum.
sections.Landmarks: Landmarks include the Eiffel Tower, Notre-Dame, and the Arc de Triomphe.

key_facts: Home of the Louvre and Eiffel Tower

San Francisco.title: San Francisco
San Francisco.summary: San Francisco is a city in Northern California known for its steep hills, Victorian architecture, and as a global hub for technology and innovation.

sections.Geography: The city occupies the tip of a peninsula between the Pacific Ocean and San Francisco Bay.
sections.Economy: It anchors the San Francisco Bay Area, home to Silicon Valley and companies like OpenAI and Apple.
sections.Landmarks: Landmarks include the Golden Gate Bridge, Alcatraz Island, and Fisherman's Wharf.

key_facts: Home to the Golden Gate Bridge
Anchors the Bay Area tech economy

Mount Everest.title: Mount Everest
Mount Everest.summary: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, located in the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and China.

sections.Geography: Its summit is 8,849 meters (29,032 feet) above sea level.
sections.Exploration: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay made the first confirmed ascent in 1953.
sections.Challenges: Climbers face extreme cold, low oxygen, and the 'death zone' above 8,000 meters.

key_facts: First climbed in 1953 by Hillary and Norgay

Pacific Ocean.title: Pacific Ocean
Pacific Ocean.summary: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of Earth's oceanic divisions, extending from the Arctic in the north to the Southern Ocean in the south.

sections.Geography: It covers about one-third of Earth's surface, larger than all land area combined.
sections.Depth: The Mariana Trench in the western Pacific is the deepest known point on Earth.
sections.Currents: El Nino and La Nina are Pacific climate phenomena affecting global weather.

key_facts: Covers a third of Earth's surface
Home to El Nino and La Nina

Sahara.title: Sahara
Sahara.summary: The Sahara is a vast desert spanning North Africa, the largest hot desert in the world, covering about 9 million square kilometers.

sections.Geography: It stretches from the Atlantic Ocean to the Red Sea across eleven countries.
sections.Climate: Daytime temperatures can exceed 50C while nights can be near freezing.
sections.History: It was once a grassy savanna and hosts ancient rock art depicting hippos and giraffes.

Amazon rainforest.title: Amazon rainforest
Amazon rainforest.summary: The Amazon rainforest is the world's largest tropical rainforest, located in the Amazon basin of South America, mostly within Brazil.

sections.Biodiversity: It houses about 10% of the world's known species and is the most biodiverse tract of tropical rainforest.
sections.Geography: The rainforest spans nine countries, with around 60% within Brazil.
sections.Threats: Deforestation for cattle ranching and agriculture threatens its ecological function.

Eiffel Tower.title: Eiffel Tower
Eiffel Tower.summary: The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower in Paris, France, built for the 1889 Exposition Universelle and named after engineer Gustave Eiffel.

sections.Construction: It was built from 1887 to 1889 and stands 330 meters tall including antennas.
sections.History: Originally criticized by Parisian artists, it became a beloved global icon.
sections.Tourism: It is one of the most-visited paid monuments in the world.

Great Wall of China.title: Great Wall of China
Great Wall of China.summary: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications across northern China, built and rebuilt over centuries to protect against nomadic invasions.

sections.History: The earliest walls date to the 7th century BC; most of the existing wall is from the Ming dynasty (1368-1644).
sections.Length: The total length of all sections exceeds 21,000 kilometers.
sections.Myth: The claim that it is visible from the Moon with the naked eye is a myth.

key_facts: Not actually visible from the Moon

William Shakespeare.title: William Shakespeare
William Shakespeare.summary: William Shakespeare was an English playwright, poet, and actor, widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language and the world's pre-eminent dramatist.

sections.Life: Shakespeare was born in 1564 in Stratford-upon-Avon and died in 1616.
sections.Works: He wrote 39 plays and 154 sonnets, including 'Hamlet', 'Macbeth', and 'Romeo and Juliet'.
sections.Legacy: His works have been translated into every major language and performed more than those of any other playwright.

Leonardo da Vinci.title: Leonardo da Vinci
Leonardo da Vinci.summary: Leonardo da Vinci was an Italian polymath of the High Renaissance, celebrated as a painter, engineer, scientist, and inventor.

sections.Life: Leonardo was born in 1452 in Vinci, Italy, and trained in Florence under Andrea del Verrocchio.
sections.Works: His paintings include the 'Mona Lisa' and 'The Last Supper'.
sections.Notebooks: His notebooks contain drawings of flying machines, anatomy, and engineering concepts far ahead of their time.

Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart.title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart.summary: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was a prolific and influential Austrian composer of the Classical period, born in Salzburg in 1756.

sections.Early life: A child prodigy, Mozart began composing at age five and toured Europe with his family.
sections.Works: He composed over 600 works including symphonies, concertos, operas, and the 'Requiem'.
sections.Death: He died in 1791 at age 35 in Vienna under circumstances that remain debated.

key_facts: Child prodigy composing by age five

The Beatles.title: The Beatles
The Beatles.summary: The Beatles were an English rock band formed in Liverpool in 1960, widely regarded as the most influential band of all time.

sections.Members: The band comprised John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr.
sections.Success: They pioneered studio innovations and scored a record 20 Billboard Hot 100 number-one hits.
sections.Breakup: The band disbanded in 1970; members pursued solo careers.

Pablo Picasso.title: Pablo Picasso
Pablo Picasso.summary: Pablo Picasso was a Spanish painter, sculptor, and co-founder of the Cubist movement, regarded as one of the most influential artists of the 20th century.

sections.Life: Picasso was born in 1881 in Malaga, Spain, and spent much of his life in France.
sections.Periods: His work spans the Blue Period, Rose Period, and Cubism, co-founded with Georges Braque.
sections.Works: Famous works include 'Les Demoiselles d'Avignon' and 'Guernica'.

key_facts: One of the 20th century's greatest artists

Vincent van Gogh.title: Vincent van Gogh
Vincent van Gogh.summary: Vincent van Gogh was a Dutch Post-Impressionist painter whose work had far-reaching influence on 20th-century art.

sections.Life: Van Gogh was born in 1853 in the Netherlands and produced most of his work in France.
sections.Style: He is known for bold colors and expressive brushwork, as in 'The Starry Night'.
sections.Legacy: He sold few paintings in his life but became among the most famous artists after his death in 1890.

Star Wars.title: Star Wars
Star Wars.summary: Star Wars is an American epic space-opera multimedia franchise created by George Lucas, beginning with the 1977 film of the same name.

sections.Creation: The original film was released in 1977 and became a worldwide pop-culture phenomenon.
sections.Films: The main saga comprises three trilogies; later eras include sequels and spin-offs.
sections.Franchise: The franchise spans films, television, books, games, and theme parks, owned by Disney since 2012.

The Lord of the Rings.title: The Lord of the Rings
The Lord of the Rings.summary: The Lord of the Rings is an epic high-fantasy novel by the English author and scholar J. R. R. Tolkien, published in three volumes in 1954 and 1955.

sections.Plot: It follows the hobbit Frodo Baggins's quest to destroy the One Ring and defeat the dark lord Sauron.
sections.Reception: It is one of the best-selling books ever written, with over 150 million copies sold.
sections.Adaptations: Peter Jackson's film trilogy (2001-2003) won 17 Academy Awards.

key_facts: Written by J. R. R. Tolkien
Quest to destroy the One Ring
Adapted into an Oscar-winning film trilogy

J. R. R. Tolkien.title: J. R. R. Tolkien
J. R. R. Tolkien.summary: John Ronald Reuel Tolkien was an English writer and philologist, best known as the author of 'The Hobbit' and 'The Lord of the Rings'.

sections.Life: Tolkien was born in 1892 in South Africa and raised in England; he served in World War I.
sections.Career: He was a professor of Anglo-Saxon at Oxford and a leading scholar of Beowulf.
sections.Legendarium: He created an elaborate fictional mythology set in Middle-earth, rooted in invented languages.

key_facts: Author of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings

Microsoft.title: Microsoft
Microsoft.summary: Microsoft is an American multinational technology corporation that produces computer software, consumer electronics, and cloud services, headquartered in Redmond, Washington.

sections.History: Founded in 1975 by Bill Gates and Paul Allen, Microsoft rose to dominate the PC operating system market with Windows.
sections.Products: Major products include Windows, Microsoft Office, Azure, and the Xbox console.
sections.AI: Microsoft is a major investor in OpenAI and integrates its models into products like Copilot.

key_facts: Founded in 1975 by Bill Gates and Paul Allen

Meta Platforms.title: Meta Platforms
Meta Platforms.summary: Meta Platforms, doing business as Meta and formerly Facebook, is an American multinational technology company that owns Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp.

sections.History: Facebook was founded in 2004 by Mark Zuckerberg at Harvard; it rebranded as Meta in 2021.
sections.Products: Its platforms include Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and the Meta Quest VR headset.
sections.AI: Meta's AI Research lab developed the PyTorch framework and the LLaMA family of language models.

Google.title: Google
Google.summary: Google is an American multinational technology company specializing in internet services and products, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc., founded in 1998.

sections.History: Google was founded in 1998 by Larry Page and Sergey Brin at Stanford.
sections.Products: Its products include the Google Search engine, Android, YouTube, and the Google Cloud platform.
sections.AI: Google developed the TensorFlow framework, the Transformer architecture, and the Gemini models.

key_facts: Founded in 1998 by Page and Brin

Sam Altman.title: Sam Altman
Sam Altman.summary: Sam Altman is an American entrepreneur and investor who has served as the chief executive officer of OpenAI since 2019.

sections.Early career: Altman was president of the startup accelerator Y Combinator from 2014 to 2019.
sections.OpenAI: He became CEO of OpenAI in 2019 and led the launch of ChatGPT in 2022.
sections.2023 board crisis: He was briefly ousted by the OpenAI board in November 2023 and reinstated days later.

Elon Musk.title: Elon Musk
Elon Musk.summary: Elon Musk is a businessman known for founding SpaceX and Tesla, and for his early role at OpenAI before departing over disagreements about its direction.

sections.Companies: Musk leads SpaceX, Tesla, and the social network X (formerly Twitter), and founded the AI company xAI.
sections.OpenAI: He co-founded OpenAI in 2015 but left in 2018 citing conflicts with Tesla's AI work.
sections.xAI: He founded xAI in 2023, developing the Grok language model.

SpaceX.title: SpaceX
SpaceX.summary: SpaceX is an American aerospace manufacturer and space transportation company founded by Elon Musk in 2002.

sections.Achievements: SpaceX developed the Falcon 9 rocket and the reusable Dragon spacecraft, and was the first private company to send humans to orbit.
sections.Starship: Its Starship vehicle is designed for missions to the Moon and Mars.
sections.Starlink: SpaceX operates the Starlink satellite internet constellation.

key_facts: First private company to send humans to orbit

Tesla, Inc..title: Tesla, Inc.
Tesla, Inc..summary: Tesla, Inc. is an American automotive and energy company that designs and manufactures electric vehicles, battery storage, and solar products.

sections.History: Founded in 2003, Tesla has been led by CEO Elon Musk since 2008.
sections.Products: Products include the Model S, Model 3, Model X, Model Y, and the Cybertruck.
sections.Mission: Tesla's mission is to accelerate the world's transition to sustainable energy.

key_facts: Makes electric vehicles like the Model 3
